notes.purpose: Carlton's note is met: a hand-built oak (oak_log axis=y trunk, oak_wood joints, an oak_log axis=z branch) with a ragged three-clump crown overhangs and shades the left bench and the back bench, with the fire ring left open to the sky
notes.artefacts: Leaves are all persistent=true and log axes make sense, but a few tree blocks join only at corners (see problems)
notes.roof: Fire pit itself has no roof (right); the new dark oak firewood shelter has a flat slab roof, a lean-to slope would read better
notes.levels: Clearly different from L2: the young oak has grown into a big shade tree with lanterns hanging from its branches, and a dark oak firewood shelter is new

visual.summary: Level 3 grows the young oak into a big custom shade tree whose branches reach over the left and back benches, with a lantern hanging from each branch, and adds a dark oak firewood shelter. It answers Carlton's shade-tree note.
problems: Three oak leaves touch the rest only at a corner and float: (x2,y4,z2), (x5,y4,z6), (x6,y4,z6); attach each to a leaf or log on a face, or remove them
The trunk bend joins only through leaves: the trunk top at (x1,y3,z7) and the bent trunk at (x2,y4,z6) meet diagonally; put oak_wood at (x1,y4,z7) or (x2,y4,z7) so the wood is continuous
The back branch (x3..4,y5,z7) meets the trunk (x2,y5,z6) only at a corner; add oak_wood/oak_log at (x2,y5,z7) or (x3,y5,z6)
Firewood shelter roof (dark oak slabs, x6..8, y2, z7..8) is flat: one row of stairs would make it a lean-to (small)
Lanterns are fine: the two hanging ones sit under oak_wood (x1,y5,z4) and (x4,y5,z7), the shelter one under a slab; standing ones are on fence posts. Flowers and grass are on the ground layer
Reachability: all ground places reached; the only unreached places are on top of leaves, which is fine
